answer: A per-identity memory-hard proof-of-work stamp: before an agent may act, it must burn a calibrated amount of compute and post a small refundable bond that pays out only after the node stays honest for many epochs. A real operator pays that once at the vertex of onboarding; a sybil farm pays it for every fake seat. Since the stamp binds a hardware quote to a distinct network island, cloning a seat voids it, so the attacker cannot wander cheaply across thousands of aliases. Faking a crowd costs compute that is never recovered, making mass impersonation irrational.
